action: No action needed; for awareness. Dam and water-infrastructure operators can watch for further word from Illinois authorities and CISA.
date_note: Monday 16 November per BNO News, which relays the Illinois Department of Natural Resources; CBS Chicago says only 'Monday'. Reported 20 November.
exec: A state-run dam in Illinois was the target of an apparent cyberattack, which shows why operators of water infrastructure keep control systems locked down.
place: Algonquin Dam, Fox River, McHenry County, Illinois
plain: Illinois officials say there was an apparent cyberattack on the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River. Staff acted at once and the dam kept running. Officials have not said how it happened.

sources.name: CBS Chicago: Illinois officials investigating 'apparent cyberattack' at Algonquin Dam on Fox River
BNO News: Illinois investigates apparent cyberattack on Fox River dam

summary: CBS Chicago reports that the Illinois Department of Natural Resources said an apparent cyberattack happened on Monday at the Algonquin Dam on the Fox River, and that staff took action to prevent unauthorized access and keep the dam running. BNO News dates it 16 November. State officials gave no further detail on the nature of the attack and said there was no indication of a link to other recent outages. Illinois State Police, IEMA, the state technology department and CISA are investigating.
title: Illinois says apparent cyberattack hit Algonquin Dam on the Fox River

validation.note: CBS Chicago and BNO News both relay the Illinois Department of Natural Resources statement; BNO appears to rely on CBS, so this is one underlying report. The IDNR's own statement was not read.
